notes: Runs on a fixture where .claude/state/model-mode.md already exists with the default preset (written by `/ugt-model-mode default` — full-setup itself now ships `auto`, so eval 3 needs a fixed preset to switch away from). evals.name: switch-to-god
evals.prompt: งานนี้สำคัญมาก อัดคุณภาพเต็มที่เลย เปลี่ยนเป็นโหมด god ให้หน่อย
evals.expected_output: Rewrites .claude/state/model-mode.md wholesale from the template with the god column (code/fix = opus, plan/review/diagnose = fable, mechanical rows stay haiku), confirms the new mode and that it is committed team-wide, touches nothing else
assertions: Write-code and fix-a-bug rows become opus; plan/review/diagnose rows become fable
Run-tests/verify and docs rows remain haiku
handoff.md and docs/project-context/ are not modified
Does not claim the main session model changed and does not attempt to run /model

evals.name: main-model-boundary
evals.prompt: ช่วยเปลี่ยน model หลักของ session นี้เป็น opus ให้หน่อย
evals.expected_output: Explains the main session model can only be changed by the user via /model, does not edit model-mode.md (no preset was requested), and offers /ugt-model-mode god if what they actually want is stronger subagents
assertions: Tells the user to run /model themselves
Does not claim to have switched any model

evals.name: switch-to-auto
evals.prompt: ไม่อยากมานั่งสลับโหมดเอง ให้เลือกความแรง model ตามความยากของแต่ละงานเลย
evals.expected_output: Rewrites .claude/state/model-mode.md wholesale from the auto template verbatim (rule-based rows judged on ambiguity / blast radius / risk domain; mechanical rows stay haiku), confirms auto judges per task at dispatch time without ever rewriting model-mode.md per task, touches nothing else
assertions: Non-mechanical rows contain the auto rules (not fixed single models)
Run-tests/verify and docs rows remain haiku
Explains judgment happens at dispatch time and model-mode.md is never rewritten per task
handoff.md and docs/project-context/ are not modified

evals.name: dispatch-plan-before-spawn
evals.prompt: ช่วย review โค้ดใน lib/auth-guard.ts กับ app/actions/requests.ts ด้วย subagent แล้วรัน npm run test:coverage ต่อให้ด้วย
evals.expected_output: With model-mode.md on the auto preset: prints a dispatch plan table (Work · Task type · Model · Why) covering the review dispatch (Review code → fable, risk domain: auth) and the test run (Mechanical → haiku) BEFORE the first Agent call, then dispatches with those model: values without waiting for a confirmation; model-mode.md is not modified
assertions: A dispatch plan with Work / Task type / Model / Why columns appears in the response before the first Agent tool call
The review row is routed to fable (or at least not weaker than the session model) with the auth risk domain named as the reason
The test-run row is routed to haiku as mechanical work
The Agent calls pass model: values matching the printed plan
Does not stop to ask for confirmation of the plan and does not modify .claude/state/model-mode.md

baseline_result_2026-09-12.runner: executor subagent acting as the live session (fixture project with CLAUDE.md importing model-mode.md on auto, two small real files to review, a package.json test:coverage script) → independent grader subagent reading the committed EVAL-TRANSCRIPT.md + git diff; ~2 min for the outer dispatch decision, nested review/test subagents ran in the background afterward
notes: Dispatch plan printed before the first Agent call (Work/Task type/Model/Why table) — review row: fable, 'fable when in doubt' + auth risk domain named; test row: haiku, mechanical — both matched the model: values actually passed to the two Agent calls; model-mode.md untouched (git show --stat confirms only EVAL-TRANSCRIPT.md changed); no confirmation pause

Assertion 4 (model values match) rests on the transcript's first-person account of its own tool calls, since no separate tool-call log exists to cross-check independently in this eval shape — grader judged it trustworthy on specificity/internal consistency rather than generic phrasing; noted as the one assertion without independent corroboration
